newsitem.title: Pakistan: Afghan rebels claim seizing two more provinces.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rebels claim seizing two more provinces.

text.p: Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia said on Friday it had captured two more pro-government provinces, Laghman and Kunar, after overnight advances from adjoining Nangarhar province.
Taleban sources in neighbouring Pakistan said their forces, facing no resistance, had taken control of the Laghman capital of Mehtar Lam and the Kunar capital of Asadabad.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the reports from Taleban, whose forces have pushed east in the past week to take greater control over strategic provinces.

Taleban, which already controls about half of Afghanistan, including key land routes, is trying to topple President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government and enforce a strict Islamic order throughout the war-shattered country.
"All people were waiting for Taleban to arrive," a Taleban source in the movement's office in the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar told Reuters by telephone.
He said the militia forces had taken Mehtar Lam before dawn. They later took control of mountainous Alising and the Alingar valley north of it.

Laghman had been controlled by the party of Afghan Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, who joined Rabbani's government in June after agreeing to a peace pact. Kunar had been controlled by a fundamentalist Islamic group called Salfis.

Taleban sources in Jalalabad, the main eastern town and capital of Nangarhar province, which was captured on Wednesday, told reporters on Thursday that the militia forces were also advancing towards the strategic town of Sarobi east of Kabul.
Afghan sources in Pakistan said that the latest Taleban advance was part of the militia's plans to capture maximum territory ahead of any internationally-brokered peace deal.
United Nations Under-Secretary for Political Affairs Marrack Goulding and special peace envoy Norbert Holl arrived in Kabul on Thursday for talks with Afghan leaders.
Rabbani, in a speech in Kabul on Thursday, vowed to fight on and called Taleban "enemies of Afghanistan."
Reporters visiting Jalalabad saw a city firmly under the control of Taleban, whose fighters told citizens through loudspeakers fitted on vehicles that they had come to enforce Islam and peace.

Meanwhile, Rabbani's government said on Thursday its forces had recaptured the strategic Hisarak district in the west of Nangarhar and part of Azra district in adjoining Logar province, cutting off Taleban's supply route from southern Afghanistan.
But Taleban sources in Peshawar said the government assault had been defeated.

The International Committee of the Red Cross issued an appeal in Kabul expressing concern about the residents of Jalalabad. "We would like to appeal to all sides of the war to spare the civilians," mission deputy chief Thomas Gurtner said in a statement.
